answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a ferrous as the anchor of the cost.
